data.name: Fataan
data.gender_notes: Fataan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'fatana', meaning 'to release, set free, or liberate'. This name evokes a sense of freedom and emancipation. The name Fataan carries the meaning “Released, Liberated” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fataan usually hope their child will grow to embody released, liberated and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Fataan is a name that represents the joy and freedom that comes from being close to Allah. It is a name that reminds us to always be grateful for the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon us, and to find joy in the simple things in life. It is a name that encourages us to be free from the hardships of this world and to focus on the eternal joy that comes from being in the presence of Allah.
data.etymology: Fataan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Released, Liberated.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fataan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fataan carries a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. It can be given to a child born during the festivity of Eid al-Fitr, which marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan and a time of release from the daily routines and worldly distractions. Thus, the name is associated with the feelings of liberation that come with this religious holiday.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Fataan can represent a journey towards inner freedom, release from spiritual bondage, or the breaking of self-imposed limitations. It can be a reminder of the power of Allah to set us free and provide us with opportunities for growth and transformation. Ultimately, Fataan can be a source of inspiration for individuals to seek their own liberation and live a life that honors their highest potential.
